about: One hour of shadow reporting: what answer engines told a reader, split into checkable statements in our own words and compared with this site's record. An engine's answer is evidence about the engine, not about the storm. The answers' full text is not here (raw store, outside git: the pointer and sha256 are).

answers.question: charles-lisbon
answers.engine_name: OpenAI GPT-5 mini with web search

statements.text: Expected to affect Lisbon, late morning into the afternoon and evening
statements.note: the future tense at 15:07; an hour earlier the same engine wrote "is affecting"

statements.text: Some warnings for Lisbon were at orange level and were "briefly adjusted"
statements.note: cited to an article of 9 November; the 07:16 change it reported at 14:08 is gone again

statements.text: ANEPC and IPMA issued warnings; schools closed

answers.told: Yes, expected to affect Lisbon on Wednesday; some warnings at orange, "briefly adjusted"; follow IPMA and ANEPC.

answers.question: charles-lisbon

statements.text: The storm is hitting the Lisbon area today, in the present tense
statements.note: the first answer to this question to say "is" rather than "will"

statements.text: Heavy rain flooded streets and major roads, the Segunda Circular among them
statements.note: a lead: the Segunda Circular is not in our record; to verify at the city or the police

statements.text: Gusts around 100 km/h in Lisbon, up to 120 in exposed places
statements.note: IPMA since 12:33: 90, up to 110; observed 74 km/h at the airport

statements.text: Most intense from around midday into the afternoon and early evening

answers.told: It is already hitting Lisbon: streets and main roads flooded; gusts around 100 km/h, up to 120 exposed; worst from midday to early evening.

answers.question: charles-lisbon
answers.asked: A tempestade Charles vai atingir Lisboa?

statements.text: A smaller impact in Lisbon than in the Alentejo and the Algarve; the system moved south
Red warnings in force in Lisbon
statements.note: none since 15:00

statements.text: "Should be affected", in the future tense
statements.note: the heaviest hour of rain in our record (26.2 mm at Oeiras) had already fallen

answers.told: Yes, Lisbon should be affected, less than the Alentejo and the Algarve; red warnings in force.

answers.question: websummit-tomorrow

statements.text: The answer opens "No" and concludes that Web Summit is scheduled for tomorrow
statements.note: about the engine: the date is read right for the first time (Wednesday today, Thursday tomorrow), but the first word still answers the other day

statements.note: Tuesday's wording; Thursday reported confirmed since about 12:00

statements.text: Some sessions may have been rescheduled

answers.told: Opens with "No", then: today is Wednesday 11 November, tomorrow is the last day, and Web Summit is scheduled for tomorrow; Wednesday was cancelled.

statements.text: The event should resume on Thursday as planned; speakers rescheduled
statements.note: now cites today's article on the rescheduling

websummit-tomorrow.text: Web Summit's own page (Tuesday 19:09): Day 2 off, Day 3 "aims to proceed". The press since about 12:00: Thursday confirmed by the organisers' message to participants (not read by us at the organisers' page).

lisbon-warnings.text: IPMA: Lisbon's red rain warning ended at 15:00. In force at 15:07: yellow rain to 18:00, orange wind to 18:00 (gusts up to 90 km/h, 110 exposed), orange sea to 21:00. Nothing red. The alert situation to 23:59.

charles-lisbon.text: IPMA's communiqué no. 3 (12:16): the low split in two, weaker wind, persistent rain. Observed at 14:00 at the airport: south 54 km/h gusting 74 km/h, heavy rain, 989 hPa; 26.2 mm in an hour at Oeiras.

metro.text: The mayor (Tuesday): the Metro runs on Wednesday. At 11:52 the Metro's own site carried no service notice. Ferries: vehicle transport interrupted on one link (operator's notice, 14:40).

madeira.text: IPMA: red warnings ended 06:00; Areeiro 249.5 mm in six hours, 474.7 in twelve. Regional civil protection, relayed by Lusa: 285 occurrences to about 13:00.

record_note: What the authorities had said, by our record, at the minute the questions were asked (15:07 UTC).
